# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 31 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_031_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 4, Chapter 1 — Chastity and Remarriage

**1** "I command you," he said, "to guard chastity, and let not any thought about another's wife or about fornication or about any such wickedness enter your heart — for if you do these things you commit a great sin. But if you always have in mind your own wife, you will never sin. **2** For if this desire enters your heart, you will sin; and if other things as evil as these enter, you commit sin. For this desire in a servant of God is a great sin. And if any man does this wicked deed, he works death for himself. See therefore that you abstain from this desire; for where holiness dwells, there lawlessness ought not to enter into the heart of a righteous man." **3** I said to him, "Sir, allow me to ask some questions." "Ask what you wish," he said to me. "Sir," I said, "if a man has a wife who believes in the Lord, and he finds her in adultery, does the man sin if he continues to live with her?" **4** He said to me: "As long as he is ignorant of her sin, the husband does not sin; but if the husband knows that his wife has sinned, and the wife does not repent, but persists in her fornication, and the husband continues to live with her, he becomes a partaker of her sin and a partaker of her adultery." **5** "What therefore shall the husband do, sir, if the wife persists in this passion?" He said: "Let the husband put her away and let him remain by himself. But if he puts his wife away and marries another, he also commits adultery." **6** "What if, sir, after the wife is put away she repents and wishes to return to her own husband — shall he not take her back?" **7** He said to me: "Certainly; if the husband does not take her back, he sins and brings great sin upon himself; but we must take back the one who has sinned and who has repented — not frequently, however. For there is only one repentance for the servants of God. Because of repentance, therefore, the husband ought not to marry again. This course of action applies to wife and husband alike."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 4.1 — the first part of the most theologically significant mandate. This passage directly addresses: (1) divorce and adultery, (2) remarriage after divorce, (3) the obligation to receive back a repentant spouse. The "one repentance only" principle here foreshadows the major debate in ch. 32.*
